verdict.rationale: OpenCode is a general-purpose coding agent with file-edit, shell/bash tool access, LSP integration, and permission-gated auto-execution, and docs show it can 'fix an issue or implement a feature' end-to-end including opening a PR — strongly implying it can perform arbitrary dev tasks like writing tests or fixing lint via natural-language requests. However, none of the evidence explicitly documents test-writing, lint-fixing, merge-conflict resolution, or dependency-update workflows as named capabilities, and community reports flag reliability issues (failed tool calls, unreliable file edits with some models) that undercut confidence in consistent execution of such tasks. Missing for 10: explicit documentation or examples of test generation, lint-fix workflows, merge-conflict resolution, and dependency-update automation, plus hands-on confirmation these specific tasks succeed reliably.
